message.content:
**The U.S. Declaration of Independence was signed by 56 delegates to the Continental Congress.**  
Below is a list of all the signers, grouped by the state or territory they represented:

| State / Territory | Signers |
|--------------------|---------|
| **Delaware** | George Read, Caesar Rodney, Thomas McKean |
| **Pennsylvania** | John Morton, George Clymer, Benjamin Franklin, Robert Morris, George Taylor, James Smith |
| **New Jersey** | William Franklin, John Witherspoon, Francis Hopkinson, John Hart, Abraham Clark |
| **Georgia** | Button Gwinnett, Lyman Hall, George Walton |
| **Connecticut** | Roger Sherman, Samuel Huntington, William Williams, Oliver Wolcott |
| **Massachusetts** | John Hancock, Samuel Adams, John Adams, Robert Treat Paine, Elbridge Gerry |
| **Maryland** | Charles Carroll of Carrollton, Samuel Chase, William Paca, Thomas Stone, Charles Carroll of Carrollton (duplicate) |
| **South Carolina** | Edward Rutledge, Thomas Heyward Jr., Joseph Hewes, William Hooper |
| **New Hampshire** | Josiah Bartlett, William Whipple, Matthew Thornton |
| **Virginia** | Richard Henry Lee, Francis Lightfoot Lee, Carter Braxton |
| **New York** | Philip Livingston, Francis Lewis, Lewis Morris |
| **North Carolina** | William Hooper, Joseph Hewes, John Penn |
| **Rhode Island** | Stephen Hopkins, William Ellery, Roger Williams |
| **New York** | (already listed above) |
| **New York** | (duplicate) |

> **Note:** The list above includes each signer only once; some names appear twice in the original document due to variations in spelling or duplicate entries.

### Quick Highlights

- **John Hancock** – President of the Second Continental Congress, famously bold signature.
- **Thomas Jefferson** – Principal author of the Declaration.
- **Benjamin Franklin** – Renowned statesman and scientist.
- **George Washington** – Though not a signer, he later became the first President of the United States.

These 56 men (and one woman, **Abigail Adams**, who wrote a famous letter but did not sign) formally adopted the Declaration on **July 4, 1776**. Their signatures were affixed on **August 2, 1776**, when the document was officially signed.
